pending_commit.commit_message: cryptohome: Load install attributes from cache file Remove the install attributes verification code path from the InstallAttributes class in cryptohomed. The code now loads the install attributes from the cache file generated by lockbox-cache during early boot. BUG=chromium:847438 TEST=Unit tests. Change-Id: I1b77e41967f0e3b0bedee4f644d47597e1696c65 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1206076 Commit-Ready: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org> Tested-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org>

cryptohome: Remove Lockbox::Verify code path InstallAttributes loads its data from the cache file now, so the verify code path is unused and can be removed. While at it, introduce a separate enum to indicate the LockboxContents::Verify() result. Reusing the LockboxError enum doesn't make sense anymore given that Lockbox no longer cares uses this. BUG=None TEST=Compiles and passes tests. Change-Id: If35074f5f4dee4b97186b67653bfb06a61b51141 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1367786 Commit-Ready: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org> Tested-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org>

cryptohome: Simplify Lockbox implementation The Lockbox class has more functions in its public interface than we ever needed, even more so after switching InstallAttributes to read the pre-validated cache file. This consolidates the functionality to retain only what is needed and only surface the error conditions the calling code actually cares about. BUG=None TEST=Builds and passes tests. Manual testing to verify install attributes locking works on device with and without pre-existing lockbox space and already-locked install attributes get loaded correctly. Change-Id: Ifb39ec9dac160364a99af9e746756f29497880a3 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1367787 Commit-Ready: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org> Tested-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org>

futility: updater: Correct HWID digest when preserving HWID Starting from GBB 1.2, a digest is stored in GBB and must be updated whenever the HWID string is changed. In shell script version of updater, the digest is automatically updated when we do "futility gbb -s --hwid=XXX", but in native updater implementation we only updated the HWID string and left digest unchanged, this leaves devices generating wrong PCR1 values. `cmd_gbb_utility` updates the digest by calling `update_hwid_digest` using vboot1 structure, so we should introduce a new vboot2 friendly function, `vb2_change_hwid`, which changes both HWID string and digest at same time. Note this has no impact for end user's devices with write protection enabled. Only changes dogfood units AU results.
